dedupe_keys.name: flexigen open source stochastic generator of synthetic electric vehicle charging flexibility datasets for v2g and v1g demand response

description: FlexiGen is a stochastic generator of synthetic datasets on electric vehicle charging flexibility, presented in a 2024 arXiv paper for vehicle-to-grid and smart charging demand response research. The paper read on 2026-09-28 explains that real flexibility data are scarce because of cost, user engagement and privacy, and that FlexiGen simulates household and office routines with configurable probabilistic variables for user schedules, traffic, charger types, vehicle consumption and state of charge. Its hourly output gives each vehicle's connection state, destination charger, estimated departure and arrival times, required charge at departure and expected charge at arrival; an example dataset for three households with one vehicle each and an office with three vehicles is analysed and released with the code. Coverage is not geographic: routines are configurable. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (arXiv paper); code licence not found (no repository located). Caveats: the example is tiny, and the probability settings behind realistic behaviour need calibration against observed data. It supports optimisation and capacity planning studies, such as generating many plausible charging patterns to test a demand response scheduler for a building or feeder. Related record: the Risvollan residential EV charging data offers observed sessions for calibration.
